title: Kitchen Hygiene Monitoring
summary: Monitor kitchen cameras for missing caps and gloves, uncovered food, open bins, spills and pests at night, with alerts and daily hygiene summaries reviewed by the chef and hygiene lead.

seo.title: Kitchen Hygiene Monitoring with AI for Hotels | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision for hotel and banquet kitchens: caps, gloves, uncovered food, open bins, spills and night-time pest alerts, reviewed by your chef.

problem.intro: Hotel and banquet kitchens run long shifts with permanent and temporary staff, and hygiene depends on habits: caps on, gloves at cold and garnish stations, food covered, bins closed and floors dry. During a large wedding the banquet kitchen brings in extra hands for the day, and the chef cannot watch every station.

pain_points.title: Hygiene habits slip during the rush
pain_points.detail: Caps come off, gloves are skipped at the garnish counter and food sits uncovered when service is at its peak.

pain_points.title: Pests seen too late
pain_points.detail: Rodent and cockroach activity happens at night when the kitchen is empty, and is found only when someone sees droppings or a guest complains.

pain_points.title: Temporary staff for events
pain_points.detail: Extra cooks and helpers for weddings and conferences do not always know the kitchen's hygiene rules.

pain_points.title: Audit evidence on paper
pain_points.detail: Hygiene checklists are filled in at the end of the shift from memory, which gives little assurance to management or an inspector.

solution.overview: We build hygiene monitoring on your kitchen cameras. Vision models check for caps or hairnets, gloves at defined cold-prep and garnish stations, aprons, food containers left uncovered on counters, open bins, spills on the floor and people in food zones without kitchen attire. At night, when the kitchen is closed, the same cameras watch for rodent and pest movement and send an alert with a short clip. Daytime observations go to a review queue for the chef or food safety supervisor, who confirms them and uses them in shift briefings. Daily summaries by station and shift support your Schedule 4 self-checks without replacing them.
capabilities: Cap or hairnet, apron and glove checks at defined stations
Detection of uncovered food containers, open bins and floor spills
Night-time rodent and pest movement alerts with short clips
Kitchen attire check for people entering food zones
Review queue for the chef and food safety supervisor, with snapshots
Daily and weekly hygiene summaries by station, shift and event

workflow.title: Map stations and rules
workflow.detail: We map cameras to stations and agree which rules apply where, for example gloves only at cold prep and garnish.

workflow.title: Monitor during service
workflow.detail: Camera frames are analysed during operating hours for attire, coverings, bins and spills.

workflow.title: Monitor at night
workflow.detail: After closing, movement in food areas is checked for pests, and alerts are sent with a clip.

workflow.title: Review observations
workflow.detail: The chef or food safety supervisor confirms or dismisses observations from the queue.

workflow.title: Act and brief
workflow.detail: Confirmed issues are corrected and raised in the next shift briefing, and pest alerts go to the pest control vendor.

workflow.title: Summarise
workflow.detail: Daily and weekly summaries by station and shift are kept as evidence for internal audits.

inputs: Kitchen layout with stations and food zones
outputs: Observation queue with snapshots and station
human_in_the_loop: The executive chef or food safety supervisor confirms every observation before it is recorded, and decides corrective actions and training. Pest alerts prompt a person to check and call the pest control vendor.
integrations: Email reports to F&B and the GM
guardrails: No face recognition; observations relate to stations and rules, not identities
Footage access limited to the chef, food safety supervisor and GM
Observations used for coaching, not automatic penalties
Camera rules reviewed when the kitchen layout changes
Clear notice to kitchen staff about monitoring and its purpose
compliance_notes: Helps evidence day-to-day hygiene practices expected under FSSAI's Schedule 4 requirements; it does not replace inspections, licences or a trained food safety supervisor.
Staff footage is handled with notice, restricted access and retention limits under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: The main kitchen or banquet kitchen of one property with existing cameras, including at least one large event day and night-time pest monitoring.
deliverables: Camera and station map with rules
Detection tuned on your kitchen footage

what_we_measure.how: Share of observations the chef or food safety supervisor confirms.
Night alerts checked against footage review and pest control findings.
Count of confirmed issues per station and shift across the pilot weeks.
Daily summaries compared with the paper hygiene checklist for the same shifts.

faqs.q: Can it work with our existing kitchen cameras?
faqs.a: Usually, if they cover the stations clearly. Steam, glare and low angles affect accuracy, so we review each camera's view and may suggest small adjustments.

faqs.q: Will it detect whether hands were washed?
faqs.a: Handwashing duration and technique are hard to judge reliably from ceiling cameras. We can flag whether people visit the handwash station when entering the kitchen, which is a useful prompt but not proof of good handwashing.

faqs.q: How does night pest detection work?
faqs.a: When the kitchen is closed, movement in food areas is analysed for the shape and motion of rodents and large insects. Alerts include a short clip so the duty manager can judge quickly.
It works best when staff are told what is monitored and why, and when observations are used for coaching. Identities are not tracked, and footage access is restricted.
